source_text: Et item: Pudenda libidine, qui licite concumbit, malo bene utitur, qui autem illicite, malo male utitur; rectius enim accipit nomen mali quam boni, unde erubescunt et mali et boni, meliusque credimus Apostolo, qui dicit: " Quia non habitat in carne mea bonum " [n204] ; et alibi: Non est libido nuptiarum bonum, sed obscaenitas peccantium, necessitas generantium, lasciviarum ardor, nuptiarum pudor [n205] ; et illud: Quod postea propagatione fecerunt, hoc est connubii bonum, quod vero prius confusione texerunt, hoc est concupiscentiae malum, quod vitat ubique conspectum et quaerit pu dendo secretum [n206] , vel alia, quibus ad hoc argumentum uti soles, memoria tua magis quam ingenio prolata sunt. Manichaeus ergo afflictus est, ut ea, quae putabat acuta, componeret, tu vero frustratus, qui putasti latere posse, quod legeras et tenebas.
pass_a_gloss: And likewise: Who lies licitly by shameful lust uses an evil well, but who illicitly uses an evil badly; for it more rightly takes the name of evil than of good, whence both evils and goods blush, and we believe better the Apostle, who says: Because good does not dwell in my flesh; and elsewhere: Lust is not the good of marriages, but the obscenity of those sinning, the necessity of those generating, the heat of wantonnesses, the shame of marriages; and that: What afterward they did by propagation, this is the good of marriage, but what first they covered by confusion, this is the evil of desire, which avoids sight everywhere and seeks a secret by being ashamed, or others by which you are accustomed to use for this argument have been brought forth more by your memory than by talent. The Manichaean therefore has been afflicted, that he might compose those things which he thought acute; but you frustrated, who thought it could lie hidden what you had read and were holding.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS libido; Blaise often sexual desire; Julian treats as created sensation, not a sin-nature
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: And again: ‘Anyone who has lawful intercourse through shameful desire uses an evil well; anyone who has unlawful intercourse uses an evil badly. For what makes both evil and good people blush is more rightly called evil than good. We do better to believe the apostle, who says: “Good does not dwell in my flesh”’ (Romans 7:18; Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 2.36). Elsewhere: ‘Desire is not the good of marriage, but the obscenity of sinners, the necessity of those who generate offspring, the heat of wantonness, the shame of marriage’ (Marriage and Sexual Desire 1.13). And this: ‘What they afterward did in producing offspring is the good of marriage; what they first covered in confusion is the evil of desire, which everywhere avoids being seen and seeks privacy out of shame’ (Marriage and Sexual Desire 1.8).

These and the other things you regularly use for this argument come more from your memory than your intelligence. Mani, then, labored to compose what he thought clever; you were disappointed in thinking you could conceal what you had read and retained.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
